cards.title: Welcome to GNPS Programme 10
cards.body: What Is This Programme?

bullets.label: Core clinical skills form the foundation of
bullets.text: Core clinical skills form the foundation of safe nursing practice. Every procedure — from taking vital signs to wound care — requires preparation, patient identification, communication, infection prevention, technical accuracy and evaluation.

bullets.label: This level is designed around the fundamental
bullets.text: This level is designed around the fundamental clinical capabilities expected by nursing regulatory bodies and national education programmes worldwide.

cards.title: Your Learning Goal
cards.body: By the end of Level 1, you should be able to perform common nursing procedures safely and respectfully, following approved standards, organisational policy and your scope of practice.

cards.title: What You Will Learn
cards.body: Throughout Level 1, you will strengthen your ability to:

bullets.label: Prepare for clinical procedures using approved safety steps
Confirm identity, consent, allergies and relevant risks
Measure and interpret vital signs accurately
Apply standard precautions and aseptic principles
Perform specimen collection and clinical measurements
Provide basic wound, catheter and device care

cards.title: Why This Learning Matters
cards.body: Clinical competence includes both the skill and the judgement surrounding it.

bullets.label: A procedure can be technically correct but
bullets.text: A procedure can be technically correct but still unsafe if the wrong patient is treated, hand hygiene is missed, consent is not obtained, or abnormal findings are ignored.

cards.title: SECTION 1
cards.body: Preparing for Safe Clinical Procedures

bullets.label: Safe procedures begin before equipment is
bullets.text: Safe procedures begin before equipment is touched. The nurse must confirm the indication, assess the patient, explain the procedure, obtain consent, gather equipment and plan infection-prevention and safety measures.

bullets.label: Correct, intact, within expiry and functioning

cards.title: Patient Identification & Consent
cards.body: Use Two Identifiers

bullets.label: Bed number, room or familiarity are never sufficient. Any inconsistency must be resolved before proceeding.
Describe the purpose, key steps, expected sensations and possible discomfort in plain language the patient understands.
Confirm patient agreement and provide opportunity for questions before beginning any procedure.
Clinical Example: Before inserting a urinary
bullets.text: Clinical Example: Before inserting a urinary catheter, the nurse identifies the patient, explains the procedure, checks allergies and confirms privacy. A reported latex allergy prompts immediate kit replacement before starting.

cards.title: SECTION 2
cards.body: Assessment, Monitoring & Clinical Measurement

bullets.label: Accurate measurement provides essential
bullets.text: Accurate measurement provides essential information about the patient's condition. Technique, interpretation and timely response are equally important — recording a number without recognising its clinical meaning is incomplete nursing practice.

cards.title: Vital Signs & Focused Assessment
cards.body: Key Principles

bullets.label: Compare results with the patient's baseline and recent trends
Repeat unexpected results when clinically appropriate
Escalate according to urgency — do not delay on a severely abnormal value
Assess the patient, not just the number
Clinical Example: A drowsy, diaphoretic patient
bullets.text: Clinical Example: A drowsy, diaphoretic patient has a low capillary blood glucose. The nurse confirms the result, assesses swallowing safety and initiates the hypoglycaemia protocol immediately.

cards.title: Clinical Measurements & Specimen Collection
cards.body: Blood Glucose Monitoring

bullets.label: Correct identification, preparation, technique and documentation at every reading
Proper sample collection, labelling, testing technique and result interpretation
Accurate recording of all intake and output, with timely review of trends
Correct containers, labelling, timing and transport according to protocol

cards.title: SECTION 3
cards.body: Infection Prevention, Aseptic Technique & Device Care

bullets.label: Many clinical procedures create a pathway for
bullets.text: Many clinical procedures create a pathway for microorganisms to enter vulnerable sites. Hand hygiene, appropriate PPE and protection of key parts and key sites are essential during wound, catheter, intravenous and enteral care.

bullets.label: Perform hand hygiene at the correct moments
Select PPE according to anticipated exposure
Gloves do not replace hand hygiene

cards.title: Aseptic Technique & Device Care
cards.body: Aseptic Field

bullets.label: Prepare equipment, protect key parts and sites,
bullets.text: Prepare equipment, protect key parts and sites, avoid unnecessary contact. If contamination occurs — stop, discard and re-establish the field.

bullets.label: Assess wound, exudate, surrounding skin, pain
bullets.text: Assess wound, exudate, surrounding skin, pain and signs of infection. Use the ordered dressing and document findings objectively.

bullets.label: Catheters, IV lines and nasogastric tubes
bullets.text: Catheters, IV lines and nasogastric tubes require securement, hygiene, patency checks, site assessment and review of ongoing need.

bullets.label: Clinical Example: During wound care, a sterile
bullets.text: Clinical Example: During wound care, a sterile key part is accidentally touched with an unsterile glove. The contaminated item is discarded, hand hygiene repeated and the field re-established — procedure does not continue.

cards.title: SECTION 4
cards.body: Medication, Mobility, Communication & Documentation

bullets.label: Clinical skills are integrated. Medication
bullets.text: Clinical skills are integrated. Medication administration, mobility assistance, patient education and documentation all require safety checks, clear communication and thorough evaluation at every step.

cards.title: Core Principles: Safety in Action
cards.body: Medication Administration

bullets.label: Confirm order, patient, medicine, dose, route,
bullets.text: Confirm order, patient, medicine, dose, route, time and allergies. Prepare one patient's medicines at a time and monitor response.

bullets.label: Assess strength, balance and cognition. Use approved equipment and techniques to protect both patient and staff.
Explain each step, check comfort, invite questions. Patients must know how to report pain, dizziness or concerns.
Record assessment, procedure, findings, patient
bullets.text: Record assessment, procedure, findings, patient response and follow-up. Timely, factual and completed after intervention.

bullets.label: Clinical Example: A patient becomes dizzy
bullets.text: Clinical Example: A patient becomes dizzy during transfer. The nurse stops, supports the patient, calls for assistance, checks observations and documents the event — completing the transfer is never prioritised over safety.

cards.title: Programme 10 Complete — What's Next?
cards.body: By completing GNPS Programme 10 – Level 1, you have built the foundational knowledge and professional behaviours to prepare, perform, evaluate and document essential nursing procedures safely.

bullets.label: International Qualified Nurse — simulation and complex clinical judgement

cards.title: GNPS Program 10: Mastering Essential Clinical Skills
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series — Level 1: Qualified Nurse

cards.title: What This Section Covers
cards.body: Section 1 focuses on the essential steps that must happen before any clinical procedure begins — from patient identification and consent through to environment preparation and risk assessment.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Prepare a patient and environment for a clinical procedure
Apply patient identification and consent requirements correctly
Assess risks before beginning any procedure
Maintain patient privacy, dignity and comfort throughout

cards.title: Patient Identification: A Non-Negotiable Step
cards.body: Why It Matters

bullets.label: Misidentification is a leading cause of
bullets.text: Misidentification is a leading cause of preventable clinical error. Use at least two approved identifiers before every procedure — every single time.

bullets.label: Bed number, room location or personal
bullets.text: Bed number, room location or personal familiarity are never acceptable as identifiers. Any inconsistency must be resolved before proceeding.

bullets.label: Approved identifiers typically include: full name, date of birth, and hospital ID number.

cards.title: Consent & Explanation
cards.body: Informed consent is both a legal and ethical requirement. Patients must understand what is about to happen and why.

bullets.label: Describe what the procedure is and why it is needed in clear, jargon-free language.
Tell the patient what they can expect to feel, including any likely discomfort.
Ensure the patient understands, agrees, and has had the opportunity to ask questions.

cards.title: Pre-Procedure Assessment
cards.body: What to Review

bullets.label: Always consider whether additional assistance or clinical escalation is required before proceeding.

cards.title: Environment & Equipment Preparation
cards.body: The right environment protects both patient and nurse. The right equipment ensures procedural success.

bullets.label: Ensure the area is tidy, well-lit and screened to maintain patient dignity.
Confirm the right equipment for the procedure — correct size, type and specification.
Check packaging integrity and expiry dates before opening anything.
Apply standard precautions: hand hygiene, PPE, and aseptic technique where indicated.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Urinary Catheter Insertion
cards.body: This scenario illustrates how pre-procedure preparation prevents patient harm in real practice.

bullets.label: Two approved identifiers verified before any action.
Procedure explained; patient agrees and questions answered.
Patient reports a latex allergy — standard kit set aside immediately.
Latex-free catheter kit sourced before the procedure begins.
Identifying the latex allergy during preparation — not mid-procedure — prevented a potentially serious adverse event.

cards.title: The Pre-Procedure Safety Framework
cards.body: Identify Patient

bullets.label: Check sterile field and functional tools.
Every stage of this framework must be completed
bullets.text: Every stage of this framework must be completed before touching the patient or opening equipment. Skipping any step compromises patient safety and professional accountability.

cards.title: Key Takeaways: Preparing for Safe Clinical Procedures
cards.body: 🔍 Safety First

bullets.label: Safety begins before the procedure — preparation is not optional.
Use two approved identifiers every time, without exception.
Clear communication builds trust and satisfies legal obligations.
Allergies, contraindications, equipment — verified before you begin.

cards.title: Mastering Essential Clinical Skills
cards.body: GNPS PROGRAM 10 · LEVEL 1 QUALIFIED NURSE

bullets.label: Section 2: Assessment, Monitoring and Clinical Measurement

cards.title: Why Accurate Measurement Matters
cards.body: Accurate measurement provides essential information about a patient's condition. A number alone is not enough — technique, interpretation, and timely response are equally critical.

bullets.label: Recording a value without recognising its clinical meaning is incomplete nursing practice.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Measure temperature, pulse, respirations, BP, SpO₂ and pain accurately
Perform respiratory, cardiovascular and neurological checks
Complete blood glucose, fluid balance and specimen-related tasks
Recognise abnormal findings and respond appropriately

cards.title: Vital Signs and Pain Assessment
cards.body: The six essential vital signs form the foundation of patient monitoring. Always use correct equipment and validated technique.

bullets.label: Always compare results with the patient's baseline and recent trends — a single reading rarely tells the full story.

cards.title: Focused Respiratory Assessment
cards.body: Breathing Pattern

bullets.label: Observe rate, rhythm and depth. Normal adult rate: 12–20 breaths/min.
Note use of accessory muscles, nasal flaring or paradoxical movement.
Check for symmetry. Asymmetry may indicate pneumothorax or consolidation.
Auscultate all lung fields. Note crackles, wheeze or reduced air entry.

cards.title: Cardiovascular and Neurological Assessment
cards.body: CARDIOVASCULAR

bullets.label: Pulse — rate, rhythm, strength and regularity
Perfusion — capillary refill time, skin colour and warmth
Oedema — peripheral swelling, pitting vs non-pitting
Consciousness — AVPU or GCS scoring tool
Pupils — size, equality and reaction to light
Scoring tools — NEWS2, GCS as appropriate

cards.title: Clinical Measurements in Practice
cards.body: Every measurement task requires correct patient identification, appropriate preparation, precise technique, and thorough documentation. Errors in any step compromise patient safety.

cards.title: Responding to Abnormal Findings
cards.body: Recheck

bullets.label: Do not delay action whilst waiting to confirm a
bullets.text: Do not delay action whilst waiting to confirm a single severely abnormal value. Patient safety depends on prompt, structured escalation.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Hypoglycaemia Response
cards.body: A patient appears drowsy and diaphoretic. Capillary blood glucose reading is low.

bullets.label: Repeat the capillary blood glucose using correct technique
Check consciousness level and swallowing safety before any oral treatment
Follow the approved hypoglycaemia management protocol
Monitor blood glucose and clinical status after intervention

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Use Correct Technique and Equipment

bullets.label: Functioning, calibrated equipment and proper method are non-negotiable for reliable results.
Every result must be considered alongside the patient's clinical picture, history and baseline values.
A single reading is less meaningful than a pattern. Track and compare over time.
Escalate early. Delay in responding to deterioration can have serious consequences for patient safety.
GNPS Program 10 · Section 2 Complete — Practice safely. Perform confidently.

decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 10 - Level 1 - Section 3 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Mastering Essential Clinical Skills
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS) · Programme 10 · Level 1 Qualified Nurse

bullets.label: SECTION 3: INFECTION PREVENTION, ASEPTIC TECHNIQUE & DEVICE CARE

cards.title: Why This Section Matters
cards.body: Many clinical procedures create a direct pathway for microorganisms to enter vulnerable body sites. Without proper technique, routine care becomes a vector for healthcare-associated infections (HAIs).

bullets.label: This section equips you with the foundational
bullets.text: This section equips you with the foundational skills to protect patients and yourself at every step of clinical practice.

bullets.label: HAIs affect millions of patients globally each year — most are preventable with correct technique.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you should be able to:

bullets.label: Use standard precautions consistently during all clinical procedures.
Choose personal protective equipment appropriate to the level of anticipated exposure.
Prepare and protect a sterile field throughout any aseptic procedure.
Provide safe, evidence-based care for catheters, IV lines and nasogastric tubes.

cards.title: Hand Hygiene & PPE
cards.body: Perform Hand Hygiene

bullets.label: At every WHO moment — before and after patient contact, before a procedure, and after body fluid exposure.
Match gloves, aprons, masks and eye protection to the level of exposure anticipated for each task.
Wearing gloves does not replace hand washing. Perform hand hygiene before donning and after removing gloves.

cards.title: Aseptic Technique: The Four Principles
cards.body: Key Definitions

bullets.label: Key Parts: Sterile components that must never be touched — e.g., needle tips, catheter connectors.
Key Sites: Vulnerable patient sites — e.g., wounds, insertion points — that must be protected from contamination.
An unattended or compromised sterile field must always be re-established before continuing.

cards.title: Wound Care: A Systematic Approach
cards.body: Assess the Wound

bullets.label: Evaluate wound size, depth, exudate type and volume, and condition of surrounding skin.
Look for redness, warmth, swelling, purulent discharge and patient-reported pain — report changes promptly.
Use the prescribed dressing, maintain aseptic
bullets.text: Use the prescribed dressing, maintain aseptic technique throughout, and document findings objectively in the patient record.

cards.title: Invasive Device Care
cards.body: Every invasive device carries infection risk. Consistent assessment and care reduce complications and support timely removal.

bullets.label: Secure catheter, maintain closed drainage, assess for signs of CAUTI daily and review ongoing need.
Inspect insertion site for phlebitis, ensure patency, replace dressing if soiled and document site condition.
Confirm placement before each use, check external length marker, assess nasal skin and document all findings.
Remove unnecessary invasive devices promptly
bullets.text: Remove unnecessary invasive devices promptly through approved clinical processes — every extra day increases infection risk.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Responding to Contamination
cards.body: Scenario

bullets.label: During wound care, a nurse accidentally touches a sterile key part with an unsterile glove.
Never continue with a compromised field — treat suspected contamination as confirmed contamination.
Perform hand hygiene again before continuing.
Re-establish the sterile field fully before proceeding.

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Protect Key Parts & Key Sites

bullets.label: Maintain the integrity of sterile components and vulnerable patient sites throughout every procedure.
If in doubt, assume the field is compromised and restart — do not take risks with patient safety.
Assess Devices and Wounds — Not Only the Dressing
A clean dressing does not confirm a healthy wound or device site. Always look beneath and around.
Advocate for timely removal of invasive devices through approved processes to reduce HAI risk.

cards.title: NCLEX Connection: What to Remember
cards.body: NCLEX-Style Thinking

bullets.label: NCLEX questions on infection prevention test
bullets.text: NCLEX questions on infection prevention test your ability to prioritise patient safety and apply the correct sequence of actions — not just recall facts.

bullets.label: Always restore safety before continuing a procedure
Advocate for device removal when appropriate

decks.title: Medication, Mobility, Communication and Documentation
decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 10 - Level 1 - Section 4 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Mastering Essential Clinical Skills
cards.body: GNPS PROGRAM 10 · LEVEL 1 · SECTION 4

cards.title: What This Section Covers
cards.body: Clinical skills don't exist in isolation. Medication administration, mobility assistance, patient education, and documentation are deeply connected — each requiring safety checks, clear communication, and careful evaluation.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: By the end of this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Apply core medication administration principles safely and accurately.
Assist patients with mobility using approved techniques and equipment.
Communicate effectively and compassionately throughout every procedure.
Record care that is timely, factual, and completed after the intervention.

cards.title: Medication Administration
cards.body: Safe medication administration begins before you reach the patient. Every step must be verified without exception.

bullets.label: Verify prescription, patient identity, medicine, dose, route and timing.
Review allergy status and any relevant clinical assessment before preparing.
Prepare and administer for one patient only, then monitor their response.

cards.title: The Rights of Medication Administration
cards.body: These core checks underpin every medication administration and are fundamental to NCLEX competency.

bullets.label: Label checked against the prescription order.
Oral, IV, IM or topical — confirm before giving.

cards.title: Mobility & Manual Handling
cards.body: Before assisting any patient with movement, conduct a thorough assessment to protect both patient and staff.

bullets.label: Evaluate strength, balance, cognition and required assistance level.
Hoists, slide sheets, transfer belts — select based on assessment.
Correct technique reduces injury risk for patients and nursing staff alike.

cards.title: Therapeutic Communication
cards.body: Communication is not separate from clinical procedure — it is part of it. Patients who are informed feel safer and are more likely to report changes in their condition.

bullets.label: Describe what you are doing and why, in plain language before and during the procedure.
Ask how the patient is feeling and observe non-verbal cues throughout.
Create space for the patient to raise concerns without feeling rushed.
Ensure the patient knows how to report pain, dizziness, or any new symptom.

cards.title: Documentation
cards.body: CORE COMPETENCY

bullets.label: If it wasn't documented, it wasn't done. Accurate records protect patients, nurses, and the clinical team.
Assessment findings — what you observed before the intervention
Procedure performed — what was done and how
Patient response — how the patient reacted
Follow-up planned — any next steps or referrals
Documentation must be timely, factual and objective — always completed after the intervention, never in advance.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Safety First
cards.body: A patient becomes dizzy during a bed-to-chair transfer. Here is how a competent nurse responds:

bullets.label: Pause the transfer and support the patient safely in position.
Alert colleagues — do not attempt to manage alone.
Assess blood pressure, pulse, consciousness level.
Record the incident, actions taken, and patient response fully.
Key principle: Completing the transfer is never prioritised over patient safety.

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Carry these principles into every clinical interaction throughout your nursing career.

bullets.label: Combine technical skill with continuous patient assessment throughout every procedure.
If the patient's condition changes, stop the intervention immediately and reassess.
Always use approved manual-handling methods and equipment — no exceptions.
Record what was done and how the patient responded — accurately and promptly.
